candidate.blueprint_locator: Health Promotion and Maintenance: assess health risks and provide preventive counseling, immunization education, and anticipatory guidance tailored to client circumstances.
candidate.blueprint_topic: Health Promotion and Maintenance — individualized pre-travel counseling
candidate.educational_objective: Individualize pre-travel health counseling to the traveler's medical history and specific itinerary, including recommended immunizations and destination-relevant food, water, vector, and infectious-disease precautions.

options.A: Use the destination, itinerary, trip duration, planned activities, health history, and immunization status to individualize vaccine, food/water, vector, and other infection-prevention advice.
options.B: Give every international traveler the same vaccine and prevention plan because destination-specific risks have little effect on recommendations.
options.C: Skip pre-travel counseling if the client feels healthy because preventive recommendations are needed only after illness develops abroad.
options.D: Focus only on routine vaccines because food, water, vector, and regional outbreak risks are outside the scope of pre-travel health counseling.

candidate.rationale: A is correct. The CDC Yellow Book 2026 describes the pre-travel consultation as an individualized risk assessment based on the traveler's health background and trip details, including countries and regions visited, timing, duration, purpose, travel style, and planned activities. Risk management can include routine and travel vaccines, food and water precautions, vector-borne disease prevention, malaria prophylaxis when indicated, and counseling about other destination-specific exposures. B ignores major itinerary-dependent differences. C misses the preventive purpose of the consultation. D omits several core travel-health risks.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Current CDC travel guidance requires individualized risk assessment and destination/itinerary-specific preventive counseling, including vaccines and exposure precautions rather than a universal travel plan.
candidate.source_document_title: CDC Yellow Book 2026 — The Pre-Travel Consultation; Food and Water Precautions for Travelers
candidate.source_locator: The Pre-Travel Consultation — Introduction and 'Assess individual risk': risk assessment incorporates health history plus itinerary, timing, duration, purpose, travel style, activities, and infectious-disease status at the destination. 'Manage risk — Vaccinations': routine/travel vaccines depend on destination and itinerary. Box 1.1.3 includes immunizations, malaria/vector risks, respiratory illness, and travelers' diarrhea/food-water counseling. Food and Water Precautions — contaminated food/water are important infectious risks and travelers should receive safe-food/water counseling.
candidate.source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)
candidate.source_version_date: Yellow Book 2026 chapters published April 23, 2025; current pages accessed 2026-08-17
